text: The lesson supplies a complete starter program. This walkthrough explains how its GPU result reaches the Console.
The GPU writes 42.0, but the CPU prints it. What connects those two steps?
say: The GPU writes forty-two point zero, but the CPU prints it. What connects those two steps?

step: The kernel runs on the GPU
text: hello is a kernel: a function that runs on the GPU. Its body writes 42.0 into output[0].
say: Hello is a kernel: a function that runs on the GPU. Its body writes forty-two point zero into output at index zero.

text: The supplied setup reserves space for that value in GPU memory. You can leave this setup unchanged.
In main, the CPU launches hello. The two ones request one block containing one thread.

step: One thread executes on an SM
text: A thread is one execution of the kernel. An SM, or streaming multiprocessor, is GPU hardware that executes its instructions.
The thread writes 42.0 into output[0] in GPU memory.
say: The thread writes forty-two point zero into output at index zero in GPU memory.

step: The CPU has a separate variable
text: The program also has a CPU variable named value. main initialises it to 0.0.
say: The program also has a CPU variable named value. Main initialises it to zero point zero.

text: Suppose the GPU write and the CPU initialisation have both finished. The copy has not started.
Pause here. Is the CPU variable value still 0.0, or has the GPU write changed it to 42.0?
say: Pause here. Is the CPU variable value still zero point zero, or has the GPU write changed it to forty-two point zero?

step: The GPU write did not change value
text: value is still 0.0. The GPU wrote to output[0], a different location in GPU memory.
say: Value is still zero point zero. The GPU wrote to output at index zero, a different location in GPU memory.

text: The cudaMemcpy call copies the GPU result into value in CPU memory.
say: The CUDA memory copy call copies the GPU result into value in CPU memory.

text: For this call, main waits for the copy to complete before continuing. value now holds 42.0.
say: For this call, main waits for the copy to complete before continuing. Value now holds forty-two point zero.

text: The CPU reads value and prints 42.0 in Console. The kernel itself did not print that line.
say: The CPU reads value and prints forty-two point zero in Console. The kernel itself did not print that line.

text: The SM executes the thread. GPU memory holds its result. The copy makes that result available to CPU code.
Back in the lesson, trace those three roles in your edited run: which code writes the result, copies it, and prints it?
